critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is now 7490 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Phase 3 added ~370 more lines inline (dues reminders, collections, minutes, December). Should be split into members/collections.py, members/minutes.py, members/december.py routers.

There is NO admin sub-tab 'members-sub-minutes'. Minutes editing is nested inside the Meetings sub-tab (minutes-editor-<mid> is opened via meeting-minutes-<mid> toggle on each meeting card). The spec referenced 'members-sub-minutes' which does not exist — current UX is reasonable (minutes belong to meetings) but worth flagging if automated flows elsewhere assume the sub-tab name.

_send_dues_reminders uses an UNBOUNDED update_one upsert on member_notices with key='duesrem:<year>:<round>:<uid>'. If member_notices lacks a unique index on 'key', in a race two concurrent calls could both get upserted_id != None and double-send. Low risk here since the scheduler is single-threaded, but worth adding a unique index on member_notices.key.

_end_memberships comparison uses string compare of ends_at <= today.isoformat() (ISO date). Works correctly for YYYY-MM-DD but will mis-sort if ends_at ever contains time or tz. Safe for current flows where ends_at is always 'YYYY-12-31'.
members_pay_link rate limit (10/5min per IP) could be bypassed by scraping tokens from DB, but tokens are 24-byte secrets_urlsafe (effectively unguessable) + 45-day expiry. OK.

/admin/members/collections POST silently truncates share to 2dp without validating duplicates (same beneficiary + kind on same day creates a second collection). Could add a dedupe check or soft warning; low-priority.
